claims.text: Surface-functional-group-dependent electronic effects govern the catalytic activity of Fe-based catalysts.
Surface-functional-group-dependent steric effects govern the selectivity of Fe-based catalysts.
Surface-functional-group-dependent electronic and steric effects govern the durability of Fe-based catalysts.
Systematically varying surface functional groups can optimize catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability.
Metal-support interactions affect the catalytic behavior of Fe-based catalysts.
Surface reconstruction affects the catalytic behavior of Fe-based catalysts.
Surface-functional-group-dependent electronic and steric effects influence reactant adsorption.
Surface-functional-group-dependent electronic and steric effects influence reactant activation.
Metal-support interactions and surface reconstruction influence reactant adsorption and activation.
Changes in reactant adsorption and activation lead to improved catalytic performance.
Surface functional-group properties and their electronic and steric effects will correlate positively with catalytic activity and selectivity.
An Fe catalyst with inert surface functional groups will have lower activity than the functionalized comparison catalysts.
An Fe catalyst with inert surface functional groups will have lower selectivity than the functionalized comparison catalysts.
The proposed relationship is limited to Fe-based catalysts with varying surface functional groups under controlled operando gas composition, temperature, and pressure.
The extent to which metal-support interactions and surface reconstruction affect activity, selectivity, and durability is uncertain.
Failure to observe a positive correlation between functional-group properties or their electronic and steric effects and activity or selectivity would count against the hypothesis.
